In particular, the repaired invariant carries Zlength(l) <= UINT_MAX into the loop-transition witness, so the mathematical increment Zlength(l1_2)+1 is in the 32-bit unsigned range and unsigned_last_nbits does not wrap. No annotation/specification repair is required by the current statements.

Nonnegativity of list lengths and the nonempty remaining suffix give 0 <= length+1 <= Zlength(l) <= UINT_MAX, so unsigned_last_nbits_eq applies with no wrap. Associativity proves the updated decomposition.

The no-wrap upper bound follows from l = l1_2 ++ tmp_list :: l0 and the repaired hypothesis Zlength(l) <= UINT_MAX.
The no-wrap lower bound follows from Zlength_nonneg l1_2 and length = Zlength(l1_2).

proof_groups.proof_strategy: Prove the invariant lifecycle in manual witness order. Initialize with l1=nil and l2=l. Advance with l1=l1_2++[tmp_list] using xizi_sllseg_len1 and xizi_sllseg_sllseg, and use the repaired total UINT_MAX bound to rewrite unsigned_last_nbits(length+1,32) without wrap. At return, derive l2=nil from xizi_sll 0 l2, convert xizi_sllseg first 0 l1 to xizi_sll first l1, and fold xizi_sll_head.
